_note: Camera-acceptance recording script (islr.evaluation.live_videos). One video per block per condition: the signs of the block in this order, hands fully down (out of frame) for ~2 s before, between and after signs; a phrase block's phrases are signed without dropping the hands inside a phrase. Signs chosen from frozen phrases07's per-sign results (2026-11-19): A reliable controls (a failure here points at the pipeline), B confusable pairs, interleaved (both members of the model's most frequent confusions), C weak or two-handed signs, P short phrases, D the two-handed signs of A–C signed one-handed as in the phone-held reference videos (baseline condition only; compare with the same signs signed with both hands in A–C). Sign A–C and P in their full two-handed form where the sign has one (asl-lex.org shows it): the PopSign / ASL Signs references were filmed holding the phone, so their signers use one hand.

conditions.1-baseline: phone upright (portrait), at chest height ~1.5 m away, even light from the front, plain wall behind; top of head to waist in frame
conditions.2-webcam: laptop webcam (landscape), seated at a desk as you would use the app
conditions.3-busy: as 1-baseline, but a cluttered background (shelves, kitchen, a poster)
conditions.4-dim: as 1-baseline, but dim room light or a window behind you
conditions.5-angle: as 1-baseline, but the phone ~45 degrees to one side, or low on a table looking up
